## Purpose Add optional lifecycle hooks so a custom model loader can react to GPU-memory-validity transitions around `Worker.sleep()` / `Worker.wake_up()`: - `on_sleep(level)` called before `Worker.sleep(level)` frees GPU memory the loader made resident. - `on_wake_up(tags)` called after `Worker.wake_up(tags)` restores GPU memory. - `reload_weights_inplace(vllm_config, model_config, model)` called from `GPUModelRunner.reload_weights()`. Returns False by default, falling back to the existing implementation, a loader that writes weights into the model itself overrides it and returns True. First two hooks are no-ops and `reload_weights_inplace` returns `False` by default, so existing loaders are unaffected. Motivating use case: the ModelExpress loader serves weights to other workers over P2P/RDMA directly from GPU memory. It needs to stop serving before that memory is invalidated by sleep, and needs to resume serving once weights are valid again. `docs/features/sleep_mode.md` documents all three hooks under "Custom model loaders". ## Test Plan Added new tests to `test_modelexpress_loader.py`: - `test_modelexpress_loader_delegates_sleep_hooks` - `on_sleep`/`on_wake_up` delegate to the wrapped loader with the correct arguments. - `test_modelexpress_loader_tolerates_missing_sleep_hooks` - no `AttributeError` when the wrapped loader predates these hooks. - `test_modelexpress_loader_reloads_weights_inplace` - `reload_weights_inplace` delegates to the wrapped loader's `reload_model` and returns True. - `test_modelexpress_loader_without_reload_model_falls_back` - `reload_weights_inplace` returns False when the wrapped loader has no `reload_model`, preserving the generic fallback path. ## Benchmark: sleep level 2 / wake up Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct, 2 replicas. One replica is put to sleep at level 2 and woken up; on wake it reloads its weights. - **Default loader:** reads the safetensors from NFS on VAST storage. The page cache is dropped between sleep and wake, so the reload reads from storage rather than memory. - **Model Express:** pulls the weights over RDMA from the other replica. | Loader | Wake up | |---|---:| | Default loader | 49.639 s | | Model Express | **7.705 s** | Wake up is **~6.4× faster** with Model Express. ---

@@ -221,6 +221,14 @@ curl -X POST 'http://localhost:8000/wake_up?tags=kv_cache'
 !!! note
     These endpoints are only available when passing `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1`.
 
+## Custom model loaders
+
+A custom `BaseModelLoader` can override three optional methods. All are inert by default, so existing loaders are unaffected. See the docstrings on `BaseModelLoader` for the exact contract.
+
+`on_sleep(level)` is called before `Worker.sleep(level)` frees GPU memory the loader made resident, and `on_wake_up(tags)` after `Worker.wake_up(tags)` restores it. Override them to pause and resume external state that depends on that memory staying valid — for example, a loader serving weights to other processes over RDMA directly out of GPU memory. Both are no-ops by default.
+
+`reload_weights_inplace(vllm_config, model_config, model)` lets a loader own the `reload_weights()` step of the level-2 flow above. By default it returns `False` and the runner falls back to `get_all_weights()` + `model.load_weights()`, which requires the loader to expose weights as an iterator of tensors. A loader that writes final weights into the model itself should override it, perform the reload, and return `True`.
+
 ## Limitation
 
 On ROCm, the virtual memory allocation on ROCm is done through chunked memory allocation. You can control the chunk size through `VLLM_ROCM_SLEEP_MEM_CHUNK_SIZE` (in MB). The default value is set at 256MB. The larger the chunk size the faster the performance. However, setting it too large will cause OOM. So if you encounter OOM when using sleep mode. Try reducing the chunk size. It is recommended to define the chunk size as a power of 2.

+    def on_sleep(self, level: int) -> None:  # noqa: B027
+        """Called before ``Worker.sleep(level)`` frees GPU memory this
+        loader made resident.
+
+        No-op by default. Override to release or pause any external state
+        that depends on that memory remaining valid before it becomes
+        invalid.

+
+    def on_wake_up(self, tags: list[str] | None) -> None:  # noqa: B027
+        """Called after ``Worker.wake_up(tags)`` restores GPU memory.
+
+        No-op by default. Override to resume whatever ``on_sleep`` paused.
+        ``tags`` is the same argument ``wake_up`` was called with. Note that
+        weight content is not necessarily valid yet at this point -- a sleep
+        that discarded it is followed by a ``reload_weights()`` call, which
+        reaches this loader through :meth:`reload_weights_inplace`.
+        """
+
+    def reload_weights_inplace(
+        self,
+        vllm_config: VllmConfig,
+        model_config: ModelConfig,
+        model: nn.Module,
+    ) -> bool:
+        """Refresh ``model``'s weights in place from this loader's source.
+
+        Used by ``reload_weights()`` when no weights are provided. Returns
+        ``False`` by default, falling back to ``get_all_weights()`` +
+        ``model.load_weights()``. Override and return ``True`` for loaders
+        that write final weights into the model themselves.
+        """
+        return False
